title: The sequencer
learned: A sequencer plays a row of steps, one per clock pulse
CV says how high each step is, GATE says whether it plays
The step knobs cover 0 to 10 V: ten octaves, so small moves are big jumps
LENGTH sets after how many steps the row repeats

steps.why: A sequencer is a row of knobs played one after another, in time with a clock. Each step gives a voltage (CV) for the pitch and a gate for the note. It is how a modular plays a melody by itself.
steps.do: The voice and the clock from the last lesson are in the rack, with a sequencer (JX-SEQ) between them. Nothing plays yet. Press Next.

steps.why: The sequencer moves one step on every clock pulse.
steps.do: Drag a cable from X2 of the clock to CLOCK of the sequencer.
steps.after: The sequencer now steps on every eighth note (watch its step lamps on the front), still in silence: its outputs go nowhere.

steps.why: GATE of the sequencer is on while a step plays.
steps.do: Drag a cable from GATE of the sequencer to GATE of the envelope.
steps.after: One note per step, all on the same pitch: the steps' voltages are not used yet.

steps.why: CV of the sequencer is the voltage of the current step. Into V/OCT it becomes the pitch.
steps.do: Drag a cable from CV of the sequencer to V/OCT of the oscillator.
steps.after: Nothing changes yet: every step knob is at 0 V, so every step plays the same note.

steps.why: Each step knob sets its step's voltage.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn the knobs of steps 1 and 3 a little.
steps.after: A melody! But it jumps wildly and sounds out of tune. The knobs go from 0 to 10 V, and 1 V is an octave, so a tenth of a turn is a whole octave, and most positions fall between the notes of a scale. The next lesson fixes that.
steps.try: Hold Ctrl while you turn a knob: it moves much more finely.

steps.why: Every step has a gate button under its knob.
steps.do: Click the gate button of step 2 to switch it off.
steps.after: Step 2 is now a rest: the sequencer still passes it, but sends no gate. Rests are what turn a row of notes into a rhythm.

steps.why: LENGTH sets how many steps the sequence uses before it starts over.
steps.after: With 8 steps on eighth notes the melody repeats every bar. With 5, 6 or 7 it repeats at odd places and shifts against the beat: a simple way to make a short melody sound longer.

steps.do: Clock moves the steps, CV is the pitch, GATE the note. Press Next to finish.
